maya (support): heads up — ACME (tenant acme-prod-2) filed a p99/p95 latency escalation. Spike started ~2026-03-16T15:00Z, p99 ~2.4-3s, some 502s. Customer attached a couple request ids: r_9a7c, r_9a7d. They see 'OOM' hints in returned headers.
jon (oncall): thanks. any recent deploys to runtime or allocator changes? which route/model?
maya (support): route `generate:v2` on prod cluster us-west-2, model `redwood-base-7b-q4`. no platform deploys from us since yesterday AFAIK.
evan (sre): pulling metrics now — I see host gpu-mem.used jump and slab_free dropping on node gpu-usw-07 around 14:55Z. KV cache size for that tenant up ~3x vs baseline.
chen (eng-runtime): KV growth + slab fragmentation = classic tail p99. can you paste sample request payload? long context?
maya (support): sample (redacted): ```{ "prompt": "<~12k tokens conversation + system instructions>", "max_tokens": 2048 }``` they said users started sending much longer threads yesterday.
jon (oncall): repro suggestion: looped requests with long context will exercise KV and allocator. maya, can you ask ACME for a sanitized repro script?
maya (support): asked — they sent a quick curl loop, pasted below. ```for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @payload.json; done```
evan (sre): got it. immediate mitigation options: 1) enable tenant active fallback routing (route tail requests to smaller model or CPU path), 2) trigger a rolling restart of one replica to force slab compaction, 3) increase KV eviction aggressiveness for tenant.
chen (eng-runtime): root cause likely allocator internal fragmentation combined with unbounded KV cache growth for that tenant. we have a hotfix config we can flip: `allocator.compact_threshold=0.2` + `kv.max_entries_per_tenant=5e6` (temporary). flipping should reduce fragmentation and reclaim some free slabs without code change.
maya (support): what's the safe rollout? will this affect other tenants?
chen (eng-runtime): safe to roll per-cluster; config is tenant-scoped. risk: slightly higher CPU during compaction passes. recommend do: step1 apply tenant kv cap, step2 enable compact_threshold, step3 watch p95/p99 for 30m, step4 optional rolling restart of single pod.
evan (sre): I'll run a targeted restart on gpu-usw-07 at 02:15 UTC if we decide. jon — can you watch alerts and be ready to rollback?
jon (oncall): yep. monitoring runbook up. I'll keep an eye on token billing anomalies too (long contexts spike cost).
chen (eng-runtime): command to apply tenant override (internal API): ```curl -X POST https://internal-admin.redwood/v1/tenants/acme-prod-2/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"kv.max_entries":5000000,"allocator.compact_threshold":0.2}'``` 
chen (eng-runtime): quick repro locally: run loop with `--long-context` and watch `procfs/gpu-mem` and `runtime/kv/entries`. eviction command we use in emergencies: ```POST /internal/evict-tenant {"tenant":"acme-prod-2","prefix":"conversation:","limit":1000}```
maya (support): I've told ACME we'll trial the tenant caps and compaction toggle and ask them to run the sanitized loop during the window.
ivy (customer success): I'll message the customer and set expectation: rolling mitigation + 30m observation, then follow-up.
evan (sre): executing tenant cap and compaction flip now (dry-run) — will report.
auto-deploy-bot: deploy started for config-change acme-prod-2 by evan — build 2026.03.16.02:21Z
evan (sre): applied. initial metrics look promising — slab_free +12%, KV entries plateauing. p99 dropped from ~2.8s to ~1.1s on canary replica.
jon (oncall): nice. leaving alert suppression for 30m; will escalate if p95 or error rate climbs.
chen (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) add a tenant-level token limit / prompt-len soft cap, 2) add automatic KV eviction when entries grow >2x baseline, 3) schedule allocator compaction nightly for high-util nodes. I'll open a design ticket.
maya (support): thanks all — I'll update the customer with the mitigation notes and ask them to confirm if their repro still triggers.
ivy (customer success): customer acknowledged, appreciates the quick turnaround.
jon (oncall): closing thread after 2h if stable. ack :thumbsup:
__notes: generated slack thread for support channel about GPU memory pressure, p99 latency, KV growth and allocator mitigations; includes short commands and action items
